Assumptions:
- Model: redwood-70b-v2 (8k context) quantized to q4f16 for production (tradeoff: ~1.9x throughput improvement vs fp16 with negligible quality drop for standard completion use cases).
- Typical prompt bundle: 180 tokens output, 60 tokens average prompt payload.
- Target steady throughput: 800 tokens/sec; burst target: 1600 tokens/sec for up to 120s windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for generation end-to-end.

What we'll deliver in this thread:
- Karthik's tokens/sec per-GPU estimates and slab sizing recommendation.
- Warm-up strategy: pre-warm lanes for heavy callers, proactive KV caching and passive prefetch during canary.
- Mutual action plan and initial commercial terms (Ben).

Folks — adding the engineering estimates and recommended topology. Sharing assumptions again so it's explicit.

Detailed assumptions (for modeling):
- Model runtime: redwood-70b-v2-q4f16 at 2x KV-cache locality vs baseline.
- Tokenization and average tokens per second baseline measured on H100 (our internal perf bench): ~220 tokens/sec per H100 for the above model (single-request steady-state, best-case batching).
- A100 gives ~140 tokens/sec for the same model/quantization in our perf suite.
- We assume safe concurrency profile: median request size 240 tokens total (in+out).

Sizing math (to hit 800 tokens/sec sustained with 1.5x headroom):
- Sustained requirement: 800 tps * 1.5 headroom = 1200 effective tokens/sec capacity required.
- H100 slab (4x H100 GPUs per slab with local NVMe): measured aggregate ~880 tokens/sec per slab (conservative sim accounting for multi-session contention).
- Recommended baseline: 2x H100 slabs = ~1760 tokens/sec capacity (gives ~1.46x above the 1200 needed — comfortable for regional redundancy & short bursts).

Burst handling and short windows to 1600 tps:
- Short burst strategy: reserve 1 additional slab in burst pool (hot spare) that can be routed to with priority scheduling + pre-warmed KV cache lanes for top 50 callers. That provides ~880 tokens/sec more during burst windows.
- Combined (baseline + 1 burst slab) gives a theoretical capacity ~2640 tokens/sec — ample headroom; practical burst absorption depends on cache-warmth on first few calls.

Warm-up / cold-start mitigation:
- Proactive KV cache seeding: for returning sessions we persist recent KV state for 30m window and warm caches for top caller IPs.
- Prefix prefetch: when we see pattern matches (same system prompts), schedule background tokenization/warmup to fill KV in <3s for heavy users.
- Canary traffic: on launch, route 5% of traffic to a warmed canary slab for 24-72 hours while gradually increasing routing percentage.
- Cold new-session mitigation: default graceful degradation — short timeout-based auxiliary model fallback (smaller quantized variant with p95 ~ 250ms but lower quality) for first 1-2 requests while cache warms.

Latency projection: with the above and 2x slabs baseline + 1x burst, expected p95 generation latency ~240-280ms under 800 tps steady, with measured p95 under synthetic burst (1500 tps) at ~320-380ms unless caller-specific caches are warm. Our routing will try to preserve SLO by moving traffic to warmed slabs before adding capacity.

Operational notes:
- Observability hooks: token-level tracing, per-call KV cache hit metrics, and per-model latency histograms.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive scale-up for 60s sustained over threshold; scale-down with 10m cooldown to avoid thrash.
- Estimated provisioning lead time for Dedicated H100 slabs: 4-6 weeks from PO depending on region.

Files attached: warmup_simulation.csv (small sim of 90-minute ramp scenarios).

If this looks reasonable I'll convert to bulletized slide for Jira ticket and Naomi can share with Jordi.
